messages.content: We are ready to start comparing Hawaii for our eight-night vacation. Look at Maui and Kauai in the second half of October. We can move the trip by several days, so I want to understand the full cost rather than just the room rate.

I can compare three eight-night windows across both islands: October 18-26, October 21-29, and October 24-November 1. Before I price them, should I assume two adults flying round trip from San Francisco, one room, and a resort with an on-site spa?
Yes. Also include the transportation we would realistically need on each island. We do not need to stay under a fixed number yet.

For Maui, the practical comparison is nonstop airfare to Kahului plus either a rental car or airport transfers and a few rideshares. For Kauai, nonstop schedules are thinner, and a rental car is the more useful assumption. I’ll price one checked bag each, taxes, resort fees, parking where applicable, and spa availability, but not meals or treatments.
That works. Show me a couple of resort levels rather than an island-wide average.

Here is the first-pass total for two adults. Maui, October 18-26: nonstop airfare about $1,176; Wailea Beach Resort about $5,440 including tax and resort fee; compact SUV, fuel, and parking about $1,065; total $7,681. Andaz Maui is about $6,710 for lodging and brings the trip to roughly $8,951. Kauai for the same dates: airfare about $1,326 with one nonstop direction and one connecting direction; Grand Hyatt Kauai about $5,930; rental car, fuel, and parking about $955; total $8,211. Ko’a Kea is about $6,360 for lodging, for a total near $8,641.
How do the later dates change that?

October 21-29 is the strongest value window in this check. Maui airfare falls to about $1,038, Wailea Beach Resort to $5,120, and local transportation remains about $1,065, for $7,223 total. Andaz totals about $8,383. On Kauai, airfare is about $1,244, Grand Hyatt lodging $5,680, and transportation $955, totaling $7,879. Ko’a Kea totals about $8,269. October 24-November 1 rises around the final weekend: Maui totals about $7,536 at Wailea Beach Resort or $8,816 at Andaz; Kauai totals about $8,092 at Grand Hyatt or $8,542 at Ko’a Kea.
The Maui advantage is clearer than I expected. Is the car really necessary there for the full eight days?

Not necessarily. If the vacation is mostly resort-based, round-trip private airport transfers plus four planned rideshare or taxi outings would be about $510. Replacing the rental-car estimate with that plan lowers the October 21-29 Maui totals to about $6,668 at Wailea Beach Resort and $7,828 at Andaz. A two-day rental booked from the resort would add roughly $260 if you want one longer sightseeing day and one flexible day.
Use transfers plus a two-day rental for Maui. Keep the full rental car for Kauai. Now compare the weather and how crowded those windows are.

With the two-day car, the October 21-29 Maui estimate becomes $6,928 at Wailea Beach Resort or $8,088 at Andaz. Late October is generally warm on both islands, with daytime highs around the low to mid-80s Fahrenheit. South and west Maui tend to be drier than Kauai, while Kauai is more likely to have brief showers and wetter north-shore conditions. October 18-26 overlaps more weekend demand at the start, and October 24-November 1 picks up Halloween-weekend traffic. October 21-29 has the cleanest midweek pattern and currently the lowest combined prices.
Please check the spas more carefully. We would probably book one treatment each, but do not include treatment prices in the trip total yet.

Wailea Beach Resort has Mandara Spa on site, with massages, facials, body treatments, couples treatment rooms, a relaxation lounge, steam rooms, and a spa pool area; the current menu shows 50- and 80-minute massage options. Andaz has Āwili Spa and Salon, with customized treatments, private treatment suites, sauna and steam facilities, and salon services. Grand Hyatt Kauai has Anara Spa, a large indoor-outdoor facility with massage, skin care, open-air treatment spaces, a lap pool, and fitness classes. Ko’a Kea offers a smaller on-site spa focused on massages, facials, body treatments, and couples services. Appointment inventory would still need to be checked for the exact dates.
Does Wailea Beach Resort give us enough restaurant choice if we do not have a car most days?

Yes. It has several on-site options covering a full-service oceanfront dinner, casual pool and beach food, breakfast, coffee, and evening drinks. The Shops at Wailea and neighboring resort restaurants are also reachable by a short walk or brief ride, so the limited-car plan is workable. Andaz has a stronger destination-dining lineup on property, but that difference does not appear large enough to offset the roughly $1,160 lodging premium unless its spa atmosphere is the priority.
What would we be giving up by choosing Maui over Kauai for this trip?

Kauai offers a quieter, more landscape-centered stay, especially if you use the car for the south shore, canyon, and north-shore drives. Grand Hyatt also has the most extensive spa grounds of these four choices. Maui gives you easier flight combinations, drier odds in the selected resort area, more nearby dining, and a lower transportation burden. For an eight-night resort vacation with spa time and only a couple of driving days, Maui is the more efficient fit; Kauai is stronger if island exploration is central.
Check whether using October 20-28 changes the recommendation. That would let us leave Sunday and come back Monday.

October 20-28 is slightly worse than October 21-29. Maui airfare is about $1,124, roughly $86 more, while the Wailea Beach Resort total is about $70 higher. With transfers and the two-day rental, the complete estimate is approximately $7,084, or $156 above October 21-29. Kauai is about $135 higher than its October 21-29 total. The Sunday departure does not produce a schedule advantage large enough to justify the increase.
Then make Maui our choice and October 21-29 the primary window. Keep October 20-28 as the backup because it may be easier for work. Which resort should anchor the next round?

Wailea Beach Resort should anchor it. For October 21-29, the working total is $6,928 for two adults: about $1,038 airfare, $5,120 lodging with estimated taxes and mandatory resort charges, and $770 for private airport transfers plus a two-day rental and fuel. Andaz remains the spa-forward alternative at about $8,088. I would next verify refundable room categories, exact resort and parking charges for the rental days, and spa appointment availability before treating either total as final.
Use Wailea Beach Resort as the lead and Andaz only as the comparison. Do not hold or book anything. Summarize the decision and the items still needing verification.

Primary plan: Maui, October 21-29, for two adults from San Francisco, with Wailea Beach Resort as the lead property. The current complete-trip estimate is $6,928 before meals, spa treatments, and incidentals: $1,038 airfare, $5,120 lodging including estimated taxes and mandatory charges, and $770 for airport transfers plus a two-day rental and fuel. Backup dates are October 20-28 at approximately $7,084. Andaz Maui remains the comparison property at about $8,088 for the primary dates. Before any booking, I’ll need to recheck live airfare and bag charges, refundable room-category totals, resort-fee inclusions, parking on the rental days, transfer pricing, and appointment availability for two spa treatments. Nothing has been held or booked.
